reconcile.connective: Defenders fuse the two reasons: Moses' own Meribah sin was provoked by the people, and his public punishment served as a warning to them — so "for your sakes" and Moses' fault are one event.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells (Skeptic's Annotated Bible) presses the plain conflict: Numbers blames Moses' own disobedience at the rock, while Deuteronomy has Moses say God was angry "for your sakes" — the people's fault, not his.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "What angered God so much that he didn't allow Moses to enter the promised land?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/angered-god.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes … on account of he and Aaron not sanctifying him at the waters of Meribah; or of some expressions of unbelief, and unadvised words, which dropped from his lips through their provocation of him …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly fuses the two reasons: 'for your sakes' is explained AS Moses' own Meribah sin, which was itself provoked by the people ('through their provocation of him') — the core harmonization of Num 20 vs Deut 3:26.

excerpts.excerpt_text: But how was he wroth with Moses for the sake of Israel? Either, [1.] For that sin which they provoked him to; see Psa 106:32, Psa 106:33. Or, [2.] The removal of Moses at that time, when he could so ill be spared, was a rebuke to all Israel, and a punishment of their sin. Or, [3.] It was for their sakes, that it might be a warning to them …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explicitly poses the contradiction question ('how was he wroth with Moses for the sake of Israel?') and enumerates the harmonizing readings of 'for your sakes' — the people provoked Moses' sin, his removal rebuked them, and it warned them — reconciling Deut 3:26 with Num 20:12.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Deuteronomy 3:25
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, explaining 'for your sakes' as Moses' own Meribah sin provoked by the people — the harmonizing reading of Num 20 vs Deut 3:26 (Haley's specific coverage of this exact pair unconfirmed, so a row-surfaced harmonizing commentator keyed to the passage is used).
